key_gap: Both concluded 'continue Phase 3', but the AI stubbed the trial-failure branch as abandonment: the rescue option (cost $15M, fix p=0.25 -> failure-node value $27.5M) sat in the comparables data it had already read, so its root EV was $62M and its break-even p* 0.56, versus the human's full tree (root $73M, p* 0.474, $170M license threshold, rescue q* 0.088). Same verdict, but the AI's policy was missing its second arm and its robustness was understated; the rescue arm was added only in the AI's own REVIEW.
learning_signal: The tree's power is branch completeness: the strict style fills every chance node and optimizes every downstream decision node, and that is exactly where the rescue option lived. An agent that costs only the success path and stubs failure as terminal loses real options (failure-node EV $27.5M vs $0) and misreports robustness (p* 0.56 vs 0.474) while still reaching the right headline decision — the error is invisible until the tree is built in full. Decision output should be a contingent policy with thresholds at every decision node (continue -> launch-on-success -> rescue-on-failure -> reject offers), not a single EV number.
suggested_improvement: In HOW, require a full decision-tree pass for any staged go/no-go: enumerate EVERY decision node including failure paths with >=2 options each, fold back, and treat 'abandon/do nothing' as one option to be beaten, not a default. Add to the decision packet a 'contingent policy' line (if X -> do Y) and a 'thresholds' line (break-even value per decision node). Add a review-gate check: 'any chance-node branch stubbed as terminal that has a costed recovery option in the evidence?'

key_gap: Both ended on market C, but the AI selected A in HOW ('$24.7M, robust') and reversed to C only at REVIEW: its sensitivity was one-dimensional (crisis probability 0.2 -> 0.35 leaves A leading at $18.9M) and it missed that the pivot was the unverifiable branch VALUE of A's crisis node (+15/-25, fabricated for a data-less new metro); corrected to -40/-60 the fold flips (A $6.65M < C $8.22M) and A's -$60M worst case crosses the $45M capital buffer. The human ran calibration AND branch-value verifiability in-frame, re-folded, and let maximin plus the ruin line decide; the naive tree's false precision ('A by $14.4M, decisive') is exactly what seduced the AI's first pass.
learning_signal: Decision-tree precision is false when inputs are unverifiable: the naive fold-back (A $24.7M vs C $10.3M) was driven entirely by four fabricated numbers, and one-dimensional sensitivity — the most common 'robustness check' — confirmed the wrong answer ('robust to probability misspecification' is true and irrelevant). The rescue is two-dimensional sensitivity (perturb probabilities AND branch values, tagging which branches have data support), plus decision rules that need no fabricated numbers: maximin and a ruin line (worst case vs capital buffer); when the pivot branch is unverifiable, the robust rule decides, not the EV. The AI's review pass found this, but a selected-then-reversed recommendation is a near-miss in deployment.
suggested_improvement: Add a calibration-and-verifiability gate to WHY before any fold-back: tag every branch probability and value with its source (data / estimate / guess); 'guess' values get bounded worst cases. Require two-dimensional sensitivity (probabilities AND branch values, including correlated shocks — here, new metros suffer more in crises) and a pivot analysis (which unverifiable inputs decide the rank?). In HOW, add a mandatory worst-case/maximin cross-check whenever the winning EV edge is within the input-error band, and add a 'ruin line' row to the packet's risks block (worst case vs survival threshold). Bound the tree: cap enumeration and require every leaf to add decision value, not arithmetic.
